The clinical picture is highly consistent with an *incomplete spontaneous abortion* at ~10 weeks gestation. Key features supporting this: (1) Gestational age aligns with the typical window for spontaneous abortion; (2) Severe abdominal pain and uterine contractions reflect active uterine expulsion; (3) An *open cervix* is a cardinal physical sign of inevitable or incomplete abortion — distinguishing it from threatened abortion (closed cervix); (4) Bloody vaginal discharge (rather than just spotting) suggests active bleeding from disrupted decidual/placental tissue; (5) Transvaginal ultrasound showing *no intrauterine pregnancy* in a patient with confirmed or presumed prior pregnancy and declining β-hCG strongly indicates either complete expulsion (but patient denies passage of tissue) or retained nonviable products — i.e., incomplete abortion; (6) Declining β-hCG confirms nonviability and ongoing trophoblastic regression; (7) Mild anemia (slightly decreased Hb) supports subacute blood loss, consistent with ongoing vaginal hemorrhage; (8) Absence of fever, elevated WBC, or adnexal findings makes infection or ectopic pregnancy unlikely.
